identity.name: Strategically Aged Sleeper-Domain Activation — Dormancy-Break DNS Burst with DGA Subdomain Fan-Out (T1568.002 / T1071.004)
identity.summary: A C2 apex registered years early and left dormant wakes as a same-day DNS query jump from below its learned baseline into the top 5%, plus a fan-out of never-before-seen DGA subdomains. Aged (not newly registered), it evades NRD blocks; Advanced DNS Security and Cortex analytics catch the dormancy-break burst and DGA fan-out as behavioral deviations, not reputation hits.
identity.description: Unit 42 documents that adversaries register C2 domains years before use and leave them dormant so the apex accrues age and evades newly-registered-domain (NRD) blocking. SUNBURST's C2 apex avsvmcloud[.]com was registered in 2018 and stayed dormant for two years before activation drove a ~165x traffic increase; Pegasus C2 apexes permalinking[.]com and opposedarrangement[.]net (both registered 2019) activated in July 2021 with a ~56x same-day increase. Unit 42's activation signal is quantitative: a strategically aged domain that held limited traffic (below its 75th-percentile activity) for months-to-years and then gains more than 10.3x its traffic increment within a single day (average increment on activation day 11.3x), jumping into the top 5% of activity. Activation is accompanied by a subdomain fan-out — an average of 2,443 newly-observed subdomains per domain activation, of which ~161 are algorithmically generated (DGA), and DGA traffic accounts for 43.19% of the burst; half of detected domains had DGA rates above 36.76%. SUNBURST exfiltrated victim identity inside DGA subdomain labels of the form DGAstring.appsync-api.<region>.avsvmcloud[.]com; Pegasus used labels such as imgdsg4f35.permalinking[.]com and php78mp9v.opposedarrangement[.]net; a phishing gateway used DGA cloaking under ui1io[.]cn (e.g. jcxivnmqfqoiopdlvejvgucpmrfgmhwdlrkvzqyb.ui1io[.]cn); level-squatting phishing apex mailingmarketing[.]net produced 47 new DGA subdomains on a single day; wildcard-DNS black-hat-SEO apex fiorichiari[.]com burst on 2021-09-29. Strategically aged domains are malicious at 3.8% versus 1.27% for newly registered domains — more than three times higher — which is exactly why an NRD block misses them and a behavioral detector must carry the load. This card exercises that detector class on the TIM plane: two ABIOCs anchor on per-apex learned DNS behavior — (a) the dormancy-break traffic burst crossing the activation multiple, and (b) the never-before-seen DGA subdomain fan-out exceeding the apex's learned subdomain diversity. Supporting validation XQL surfaces both deviations against the real published IOC apexes, and a correlation rule stitches the two ABIOCs on the same apex within the activation window into a single strategically-aged-sleeper-domain-activation incident the DC presents as proof that Cortex caught an aged, reputation-clean C2 domain that no NRD control would have flagged.

campaigns: SUNBURST / SolarWinds supply-chain intrusion (aged C2 avsvmcloud[.]com, 2020)
Pegasus spyware infrastructure (aged C2 permalinking[.]com / opposedarrangement[.]net, activated 2021)

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-TIM-003 — Strategically aged sleeper-domain activation (dormancy-break DNS burst + DGA subdomain fan-out) for Cortex Advanced DNS Security / analytics ABIOC validation

prerequisites.description: DNS resolution tooling present so the step can emit query telemetry (dig from bind-tools / dnsutils).
DNS telemetry reaches Cortex — Advanced DNS Security (pan_dns) or NGFW DNS logs are onboarded so per-apex query volume and subdomain fan-out are observable.
prerequisites.check_command: echo 'confirm pan_dns / Advanced DNS Security ingestion in the tenant'

payload.code:
# Non-destructive: emit DNS query telemetry that models a strategically aged
# sleeper-domain waking up. Queries go ONLY to the lab-controlled resolver
# (${DNS_RESOLVER}); no data is encrypted, deleted, or exfiltrated. A SAFE-MODE
# marker records the simulated activation.
set -euo pipefail
RESOLVER="${DNS_RESOLVER:-127.0.0.1}"
APEX="${SLEEPER_APEX:-avsvmcloud.com}"
mkdir -p /tmp/cortexsim-tim-003
echo "SAFE-MODE simulated sleeper-domain activation of ${APEX} at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)" > /tmp/cortexsim-tim-003/activation.marker
# (a) dormancy-break burst: spike apex query volume into the top-5% band
for i in $(seq 1 120); do dig +short +time=1 +tries=1 "@${RESOLVER}" "${APEX}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done
# (b) DGA subdomain fan-out: never-before-seen high-entropy labels under the apex
for pub in imgdsg4f35 php78mp9v dga1a2b3c appsync-api-70e2b8f4; do dig +short +time=1 +tries=1 "@${RESOLVER}" "${pub}.${APEX}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done
for i in $(seq 1 60); do sub=$(head -c 16 /dev/urandom | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n'); dig +short +time=1 +tries=1 "@${RESOLVER}" "${sub}.${APEX}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done
echo '[CortexSim] SIM-TIM-003 dormancy-break burst + DGA fan-out emitted'

input_variables.description: Lab-controlled resolver the modeled queries are sent to. Keep this a sinkhole / lab zone so no query reaches real (sinkholed) attacker infrastructure.

input_variables.name: SLEEPER_APEX
input_variables.description: The strategically aged apex whose dormancy break is being modeled (published SUNBURST C2 apex, now sinkholed).

abiocs.name: Dormancy-Break Traffic Burst on a Strategically Aged Domain
abiocs.description: An apex domain whose learned DNS query-volume baseline — a per-apex average daily query count computed over a 90-day baseline window while the apex held below its 75th-percentile activity — is suddenly exceeded by the activation-day volume by more than 10.3x, jumping into the top-5% band. The activation multiple is measured against that learned multi-day average (over the explicit 90-day window, excluding the activation day) rather than against an adjacent in-window bucket, so a prior baseline window must exist (a hard precondition) and the detector fires on aged, reputation-clean C2 apexes (SUNBURST/Pegasus lineage) that a newly-registered-domain block cannot see. Statistical baseline-deviation detector.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = pan_dns
| filter dns_query_name != null and _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 7776000)
| alter apex_domain = arrayindex(regextract(lowercase(dns_query_name), "([a-z0-9_-]+\.[a-z]+)$"), 0)
| alter day_bucket = format_timestamp("%Y-%m-%d", _time)
| alter is_activation_day = if(_time >= to_timestamp(current_time() - 86400), 1, 0)
| comp count() as day_query_count by apex_domain, day_bucket, is_activation_day
| comp sum(if(is_activation_day = 1, day_query_count, 0)) as activation_day_queries, avg(if(is_activation_day = 0, day_query_count, null)) as baseline_daily_avg, count_distinct(if(is_activation_day = 0, day_bucket, null)) as baseline_days by apex_domain
| filter baseline_days >= 1 and baseline_daily_avg > 0
| alter activation_multiple = divide(activation_day_queries, baseline_daily_avg)
| filter activation_multiple >= 10.3
| sort desc activation_multiple
| fields apex_domain, baseline_days, baseline_daily_avg, activation_day_queries, activation_multiple
abiocs.causality_anchor: Per-apex learned DNS request-volume baseline — a 90-day average daily query count accrued while the apex held below its 75th-percentile activity for months-to-years — compared against the activation-day volume; the >10.3x activation multiple is measured against that learned average, not against an adjacent in-window bucket, so it anchors to the apex's own months-to-years history rather than to domain reputation.

abiocs.name: Never-Before-Seen DGA Subdomain Fan-Out Under a Newly-Activated Apex
abiocs.description: Under a single apex, a burst of distinct, high-entropy, never-before-seen subdomain labels appears within the activation window — the DGA fan-out Unit 42 measures at an average 161 DGA subdomains per activation (43.19% of burst traffic). The ABIOC anchors on the per-apex learned subdomain-diversity baseline and a label character-class/entropy gate: the left-most label must be an alphanumeric string of length >= 8 carrying >= 2 digits (a DGA/high-entropy shape that pure-dictionary subdomains like `login` or `api` fail, but the cited 9-10 char Pegasus labels imgdsg4f35 / php78mp9v clear), and known-benign CDN/cloud apexes (cloudfront.net, amazonaws.com, akamai*, azurefd.net, googleusercontent.com, cloudflare.net) are excluded so long benign labels do not roll up as a false fan-out. It fires when the count of distinct qualifying never-before-seen labels under one apex exceeds the apex's learned diversity. It catches identity-in-the-subdomain exfiltration (SUNBURST DGAstring.appsync-api.<region>.avsvmcloud[.]com) and DGA-cloaked phishing that no static IOC list enumerates.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = pan_dns
| filter dns_query_name != null
| alter apex_domain = arrayindex(regextract(lowercase(dns_query_name), "([a-z0-9_-]+\.[a-z]+)$"), 0)
| filter apex_domain not in ("cloudfront.net", "amazonaws.com", "akamaiedge.net", "akamai.net", "azurefd.net", "googleusercontent.com", "cloudflare.net")
| alter leftmost_label = arrayindex(split(lowercase(dns_query_name), "."), 0)
| filter leftmost_label ~= "^[a-z0-9]{8,}$"
| alter label_digit_count = array_length(regextract(leftmost_label, "[0-9]"))
| filter label_digit_count >= 2
| comp count_distinct(dns_query_name) as distinct_dga_subdomains, count() as dga_query_volume by apex_domain
| filter distinct_dga_subdomains >= 50
| sort desc distinct_dga_subdomains
| fields apex_domain, distinct_dga_subdomains, dga_query_volume
abiocs.causality_anchor: Per-apex learned subdomain-diversity + label character-class/entropy baseline -> activation-window fan-out of distinct never-before-seen high-entropy labels (alphanumeric, length >= 8, >= 2 digits) exceeding the learned diversity, with known-benign CDN/cloud apexes excluded, anchored to the same apex that broke dormancy.

xql_queries.name: Sleeper-Domain Activation Burst Surfaced in DNS Telemetry
xql_queries.query:
dataset = pan_dns
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 900)
| filter dns_query_name != null
| alter apex_domain = arrayindex(regextract(lowercase(dns_query_name), "([a-z0-9_-]+\.[a-z]+)$"), 0)

| comp count() as activation_queries by apex_domain
| filter activation_queries >= 1
| sort desc activation_queries

| alter apex_domain = arrayindex(regextract(lowercase(dns_query_name), "([a-z0-9_-]+\.[a-z]+)$"), 0)

correlation_rules.name: Strategically Aged Sleeper-Domain Activation — Burst + DGA Fan-Out Stitch
correlation_rules.logic: ABIOC(Dormancy-Break Traffic Burst on a Strategically Aged Domain) AND ABIOC(Never-Before-Seen DGA Subdomain Fan-Out Under a Newly-Activated Apex) — fuses the same-day dormancy-break traffic burst and the never-before-seen DGA subdomain fan-out on the SAME apex_domain within the activation window into a single strategically-aged-sleeper-domain-activation incident, anchored to the aged apex the newly-registered-domain block never flagged.

threat_scenarios.name: Strategically Aged Sleeper-Domain Activation Detection via Behavioral DNS Analytics
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex Advanced DNS Security and XSIAM analytics detect an aged, reputation-clean C2 apex waking from dormancy — a same-day traffic burst into the top-5% band plus a fan-out of never-before-seen DGA subdomains — where a newly-registered-domain block sees nothing because the domain is years old.

threat_steps.objective: The dormancy-break traffic burst on a strategically aged apex is detected as a behavioral deviation from the apex's learned volume baseline.
preconditions: DNS telemetry (pan_dns / Advanced DNS Security) onboarded to the tenant.

A prior 90-day baseline window has elapsed during which the apex held below-75th-percentile activity, so a per-apex average-daily-query baseline exists. This is a HARD precondition: the ABIOC measures the activation multiple against that learned multi-day average, not against traffic emitted inside the run window, so the baseline must predate the simulated activation.
steps: Emit a same-day burst of DNS queries for the aged apex crossing the >10.3x activation multiple.
Observe the dormancy-break ABIOC fire and the activation-burst validation query return the apex.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Dormancy-Break Traffic Burst on a Strategically Aged Domain` fires on the aged apex.
XQL `Sleeper-Domain Activation Burst Surfaced in DNS Telemetry` returns >= 1 row for the apex.

threat_steps.objective: The never-before-seen DGA subdomain fan-out under the activated apex is detected as exceeding the apex's learned subdomain diversity.
preconditions: The apex activation from TC-TIM-003A has occurred.
steps: Emit a fan-out of distinct high-entropy DGA subdomains under the activated apex.
Observe the DGA-fan-out ABIOC fire and the fan-out validation query return the apex.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Never-Before-Seen DGA Subdomain Fan-Out Under a Newly-Activated Apex` fires.
XQL `DGA Subdomain Fan-Out Surfaced Under an Activated Apex` returns >= 1 row for the apex.

threat_steps.objective: The two behavioral deviations stitch into a single sleeper-domain-activation incident on the same apex.
preconditions: Both ABIOCs from TC-TIM-003A and TC-TIM-003B have fired on the same apex within the activation window.
steps: Observe CR-TIM-0003 raise one stitched incident.
success_criteria: Correlation CR-TIM-0003 raises exactly one strategically-aged-sleeper-domain-activation incident anchored to the aged apex.

preventive_controls: Do not rely on newly-registered-domain (NRD) blocking alone — strategically aged domains are malicious at 3.8% vs 1.27% for NRDs and defeat age-based allow-listing by design.
Enable Advanced DNS Security to inline-block DGA and DNS-tunneling query patterns rather than only alerting on them.
Sinkhole and rate-limit resolution to apexes exhibiting a sudden dormancy-break burst pending analyst review.
detection_engineering: Let Cortex learn a per-apex DNS request-volume baseline and alert on a same-day jump past the >10.3x activation multiple into the top-5% band, independent of domain reputation or age.
Alert on a per-apex fan-out of distinct never-before-seen high-entropy left-most labels exceeding the apex's learned subdomain diversity (the DGA fan-out).
Stitch the dormancy-break burst and the DGA fan-out on the same apex within the activation window into a single incident so the aged-domain activation is one alert, not two weak signals.
